title: Electroporation of Aurantiochytrium limacinum (ATCC MYA-1381)
author: Mariana Rius
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.qjcduiw
materials: For electroporation reactions in which linear DNA plasmid will be used: Linearize 10ug of plasmid for each electroporation reaction and clean using PCR purification (QIAGEN) eluting to ~12 ul*. For electroporation reactions in which circular DNA plasmid will be used: Concentrate DNA to 1ug/ul by PCR purification (QIAGEN) eluting to ~12 ul*. *~2 to 3 ul elution buffer will be bound to spin column, elution of 12 - 13 ul will result in final volume ~10ul.

steps.title: Prepare preculture and main culture
steps.instruction: Inoculate 4 ml GPY (0.5 % yeast extract, 1 % peptone, 3 % D‑+‑glucose, 1.8 % instant ocean) with a colony of Aurantiochytrium limacinum (ATCC MYA‑1381) and incubate overnight at 28 °C in the outermost ring of a spinning drum. Use this preculture to inoculate 46 ml GPY in a 250 ml flask and culture for 3–4 days at 28 °C, 171 rpm.

steps.title: Count cells and prepare suspension
steps.instruction: Dilute 100 µl of culture in 900 µl water, load 10 µl on a hemocytometer, let cells settle 2–5 min and count; expected density ≈5 × 10⁻⁴ cells/µl (≈5 × 10⁻⁷ cells/ml). For each electroporation, transfer 1.5 ml culture to a microcentrifuge tube, centrifuge 5 min at 4 °C, 11 000 rpm and decant. Add 500 µl chilled 1X BSS (10 mM KCl, 10 mM NaCl, 3 mM CaCl₂), centrifuge 5 min at 4 °C, 11 000 rpm, decant. Add 500 µl chilled 50 mM sucrose, centrifuge, decant. Repeat the 500 µl sucrose wash once more. Finally add 100 µl chilled 50 mM sucrose and resuspend by scraping the cell mass from the tube wall and vortexing.

steps.title: Add DNA and incubate on ice
steps.instruction: Add 10 µl (10 µg) DNA to the resuspended cells (or 10 µl elution buffer for a no‑DNA control) and incubate on ice for 5 min. Transfer the mixture to a chilled 0.2 cm electroporation cuvette (Bio‑Rad) and keep on ice.

steps.title: Electroporate cells
steps.instruction: Dry the electrodes, load the cuvette into the electroporation chamber, set the Gene Pulser (Bio‑Rad) to 0.45 kV, 125 µF, 1000 Ω, clear the area and deliver the pulse. Record the time constant (τ ≈ 4–6 ms). Remove the cuvette and return it to ice; repeat for all samples.

steps.title: Recover cells in GPYS media
steps.instruction: Label a microcentrifuge tube for each electroporated sample, add 1 ml GPYS media (3 % glucose, 0.6 % peptone, 0.2 % yeast extract, 50 mM sucrose, 1.8 % instant ocean) to the cuvette, transfer the entire volume to the tube and incubate at 28 °C for 1 h without shaking.

steps.title: Harvest and plate transformed cells
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the recovered culture 5 min at room temperature, 11 000 rpm, remove 1 ml supernatant and resuspend the pellet by scraping and vortexing. Plate the remaining volume (≈80 % mortality). For dilution: from ~7.5 × 10⁷ cells in ~100 µl, take 10 µl into 990 µl ½ ASW or GPYS (100×, ≈7.5 × 10⁴ cells), then take 10 µl of this into 90 µl ½ ASW or GPYS (10×, ≈7.5 × 10³ cells) and plate the full 100 µl. For the no‑DNA control, plate cells on GPYS zeocin/amp plates as a negative control. Calculate survivorship using the diluted control plate grown on GPYS without antibiotic.

steps.title: Incubate plates and assess colonies
steps.instruction: Incubate GPYS plates (no antibiotic) for 2 days; colonies should appear. Transformant colonies will appear on selective plates (GPYS zeocin/amp) after 3–5 days. Streak transformant colonies onto GPYS zeocin/amp plates, monitor transformation efficiency, and include wild‑type controls for comparison.

steps.title: Prepare media and solutions
steps.instruction: Prepare GPYS media (3 % glucose, 0.6 % peptone, 0.2 % yeast extract, 50 mM sucrose, 1.8 % instant ocean). Make GPYS agar plates with 2 % agar containing ampicillin (100 µg/ml) or zeocin (100 µg/ml) plus ampicillin (100 µg/ml). Prepare 1X BSS (10 mM KCl, 10 mM NaCl, 3 mM CaCl₂) and a 50 mM sucrose solution. Sterilize all solutions by autoclave or filter sterilization as appropriate.
